methods.label: Pair the integers and use the mean
methods.explanation:
Pair the integers from opposite ends: \(1+99=100\), \(2+98=100\), and so on through \(49+51=100\). These are \(49\) pairs, with \(50\) left in the middle. Every integer from \(1\) through \(99\) is used exactly once, so
\[1+2+\cdots+99=49\cdot100+50=4950.\]
Including \(x\), there are \(100\) numbers. Their sum equals their average times their count, giving
\[4950+x=100(100x)=10000x.\]
Subtracting \(x\) yields \(9999x=4950\), and therefore
\[x=\frac{4950}{9999}=\frac{99\cdot50}{99\cdot101}=\boxed{\frac{50}{101}}.\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
